text:
sarah.prod: @here paging — after the canary push (v2026.03.15-canary) we've got p95 ~1s but p99s shooting to 6-8s and a cascade of 502/504s at the edge. lots of customer 5xxs in the last 3m. incident-bot: ALERT: service=api-gateway severity=page metric=p99_latency threshold=5000ms value=6800ms. mike-oncall: oncall -> grabbing logs and canary pods. can anyone confirm the deploy changes? sarah.prod: deploy included gateway mux change + new keepalive defaults from james's PR. james-eng: yep changed grpc connection pool defaults to reduce idle connections — thought it would help, not hurt. i rolled the config into the canary. olga-sre: first glance at traces — timeouts originate at gateway -> inference-proxy step. lots of connection resets (RST) and long queue times. looks like upstream servers are saturating CPU at 100%. priya-support: multiple customers just reported degraded responses to SSO flows. escalating on support side. mike-oncall: ok, mitigation options: 1) rollback canary 2) throttle canary traffic 3) route traffic away from canary to stable region 4) bump pool sizes. i vote rollback to stop customer impact immediately. sarah.prod: agree. initiate rollback and notify customers. deploy-bot: Deploy event: v2026.03.15-canary -> rollout started at 3275123462 by james-eng. mike-oncall: executing rollback command now: ```bash
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/api-gateway --to-revision=2026.03.14-stable
``` mike-oncall: rollback in progress. monitoring logs. olga-sre: starting temporary circuit-breaker tweak to reduce retries: set gateway.retry.max=1 and gateway.circuit.tripping=5xx_count(30s) -> open. james-eng: pushing a hotfix to remove keepalive change from config — but let's let rollback finish first. sarah.prod: @priya-support draft customer message: "We're investigating elevated errors and timeouts after a canary deploy; rolling back now and will provide ETA within 30 minutes." priya-support: sending out initial banner and opening ticket for affected customers. incident-bot: NOTIFICATION: rollback completed at 3275123568. service=api-gateway status=rolled-back to v2026.03.14-stable. olga-sre: after rollback p95 ~450ms, p99 dropped to ~900ms, 5xx rate back to baseline. still seeing occasional spikes on a handful of pods — probably warmup/conn-drain. mike-oncall: confirming health checks passing, no new pages. i left extra logging on inference-proxy to capture conn metrics for 20m. james-eng: reproduction notes: when keepalive lowered, connection churn increased under multiplexed grpc -> pool exhaustion -> queue growth -> backpressure at gateway. i have a small PR to revert the keepalive changes and alter pool sizing heuristics. sarah.prod: good. next steps: 1) capture logs/trace IDs for 2 customers and add to postmortem 2) leave canary disabled until we test revert in staging 3) run traffic profile test for mux/keepalive combos 4) prepare release with revert + pool increase. olga-sre: filing incident ticket and setting sev=2 postmortem. will include graphs: p95/p99, connection resets, cpu saturation, pod restarts. priya-support: customers notified with status update and will follow up once postmortem ready. mike-oncall: handing off monitoring to olga for night; i'm available for call if anything re-fires. olga-sre: took the handoff — i'll keep an eye for recurrence and collect the extra traces. sarah.prod: thanks all. add any leftover traces or relevant snippets here. james-eng: paste of the critical grep i used for resets: ```
kubectl logs -n prod svc-inference-proxy -c proxy | grep "RST" | tail -n 50
# saw ~120 RST in 2m at canary hosts
``` mike-oncall: note for postmortem: consider adding automated canary rollback threshold for p99>2s for >2m to avoid manual pages. sarah.prod: agreed — also add a test in CI that simulates high-multiplex churn so we don't regress this. incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: summary=canary induced keepalive/pool misconfig -> upstream pool saturation -> p99/timeouts -> rollback resolved impact. final status: recovered. last update at 3275123720. :white_check_mark:
